Oh. Do you know, you don't half go far on your radio, don't ya?
Well, arse and piss and C-[bleep]-T.
I didn't- I don't say- Yeah, no, it's all bleeped out. It's all electronically, er, cleaned up.
Yeah, I know. You take it steady. I didn't bring you up that way.
Yeah, well, I got it from you. You used to F and C all over the place when I was little.
Well, you used to- You used to come in-
-with a bottle of gin in one hand and a cigar in the other.
Yeah, no. You- From bingo, right? You used to come in with a vicar.
Nick his sherry. You used to come in effing and blinding. You know, I'm five years old, how am I meant to be-
And I used to correct you in every way you spoke.
You didn't learn a lot. You've got the real old Berkshire accent.
Well, yeah, I wonder where that came from.
And that other bloke, tell him your handle is Ricky.
So correct him when he's on the radio.
Yeah. Do you want to give him a message? Because I'm taping this.
He said, do you want to give him a message? Because I'm taping this.

Oh, you've gotta be Ricky Gervay! My mummy says it's gotta be Ricky Gervay!

Steve, don't call me Gervayz any more, it's Ricky Gervay!
Honestly, you don't want to wind her up.
What's all that nonsense about handle? Your handle is Ricky Gervais. Handel? What's she talking about?

You know, doing a bit of gardening and talking about crazy paving.

Ricky Gervais is my son on XFM.

I'm fine. You try and read it go on.
